answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond — like copper wiring a circuit closed — before it may transact. The bond is not a fee: it is slashed when peers prove fraud, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand bonds, while one honest agent pays once. Reputation then accrues like marble in a ledger: heavy, slow to carve, impossible to fake overnight, so a fresh nebula of spun-up accounts cannot outvote long-standing agents whose history is publicly auditable. Sybil attacks become a budgeting problem, not a scripting problem.
